quiz.title: Matrices Exercise 3.3 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on transpose, symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices and the properties from Exercise 3.3. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths, Matrices Exercise 3.3 (transpose of a matrix)

questions.q: If A is a 3 × 4 matrix, what is the order of its transpose A'?
questions.explanation: Transposing swaps rows and columns, so an m × n matrix becomes n × m. Here 3 × 4 becomes 4 × 3.

questions.q: A square matrix A is symmetric when:
questions.explanation: A matrix is symmetric if it equals its own transpose, that is A' = A, so a<sub>ij</sub> = a<sub>ji</sub> for all i, j.

questions.q: For a skew-symmetric matrix, every diagonal entry must be:
questions.explanation: Skew-symmetric means A' = −A, so a<sub>ii</sub> = −a<sub>ii</sub>, which forces 2a<sub>ii</sub> = 0, hence every diagonal entry is 0.

questions.q: Which identity does Exercise 3.3 establish for the transpose of a product?
questions.explanation: The transpose of a product reverses the order: (AB)' = B'A'. The order of the factors is switched.

questions.q: The matrix A + A' is always:
questions.explanation: Take the transpose: (A + A')' = A' + A = A + A'. Since it equals its own transpose, A + A' is symmetric.

questions.q: The matrix A − A' is always:
questions.explanation: (A − A')' = A' − A = −(A − A'), which is the skew-symmetric condition, so A − A' is skew-symmetric.

questions.q: Any square matrix A can be written as the sum of:
options: a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix
a diagonal and an identity matrix
questions.explanation: A = ½(A + A') + ½(A − A'). The first part is symmetric and the second is skew-symmetric, and this decomposition is unique.

questions.q: For a scalar k, which statement about transpose is correct?
questions.explanation: A scalar multiple passes straight through the transpose: (kA)' = kA'. Multiplying every entry by k does not change how rows and columns swap.

faq.q: What does Exercise 3.3 of NCERT Class 12 Matrices cover?
faq.a: It covers the transpose of a matrix and its properties — (A')' = A, (kA)' = kA', (A + B)' = A' + B', (AB)' = B'A' — and uses them to study symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices.

faq.q: What is the difference between a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix?
faq.a: A symmetric matrix satisfies A' = A, so entries mirror across the diagonal. A skew-symmetric matrix satisfies A' = −A, which also forces every diagonal entry to be 0.

faq.q: Why can every square matrix be split into symmetric and skew-symmetric parts?
faq.a: Because A = ½(A + A') + ½(A − A'). The first bracket is always symmetric and the second is always skew-symmetric, so the split works for any square matrix and is unique.

faq.q: Is (AB)' equal to A'B' or B'A'?
faq.a: It is B'A'. The transpose of a product reverses the order of the factors. Writing A'B' is one of the most common mistakes in this exercise.
